My starting routine
The same 4 steps for every question
READ
What is inside the modulus? What is on the other side?
SPLIT
Write two cases: inside = + right side, inside = − right side.
SOLVE
Solve each case on its own.
CHECK
Put every answer back into the original equation.

QuestionWatch forExample
Q 1 i, Q 2 d–fThe right side contains x: it must not be negative.2x − 5 = x needs x ≥ 0.
Q 1 d–hClear the fraction after you split into two cases.x − 14 = 6 means x − 14 = 6 or −6.
Q 2 a–cx cannot make a bottom equal to 0.x ≠ −3 in Q 2 a.
Q 3A quadratic in each case can give up to four candidates.Solve both cases, then test each root.

6
Try one first, with Dyna
Solve  x + 3 = 2x.
x =
Before you open a hint, write your plan in one line:
Hint 1 · Echo
Say it in your own words: “x + 3 is 2x away from 0.” A distance cannot be negative, so 2x ≥ 0.
Hint 2 · Slicer
Split into two cases: x + 3 = 2x and x + 3 = −2x. Solve each one.
Hint 3 · Roots
Ask why you must check: one case may give a value that makes the right side negative.
YOUR TURN
Test both answers in the original equation. Which one survives?
Use the hints one at a time. Try on your own before you read the next one.
Before you start
Read Section 1.4 of the coursebook: modulus functions, the definition of |x|, and Worked example 6.
Challenge ahead
Q 4 asks where a line meets a modulus curve. A quick sketch tells you how many crossings to expect.
